thread.title: Apple Becomes First Company To Hit $1 Trillion Market Cap

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Becomes First Company To Hit $1 Trillion Market Cap
text:
Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) on Thursday performed the unprecedented feat of achieving a market capitalization of $1 trillion.
X Apple shares rose 2.9% to 207.39 on the stock market today . The company ended the regular session with a market cap of $1.002 trillion.
In intraday trading, Apple stock notched a record high of 208.38, which gave it a market value of $1.006 billion.
Apple has been on a tear since posting better-than-expected June-quarter results late Tuesday.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple Stock Added To Leaderboard "Today Apple became the first company in history to reach a $1 trillion market cap," said Gene Munster, a longtime Apple analyst and current managing partner at Loup Ventures. "This valuation is driven by Apple's higher purpose to enrich people's lives. The company has been steadfast in its focus on the user."
In a blog post , Munster said he still sees "meaningful upside" to Apple stock thanks to the growth of the company's services business.
Investor's Business Daily added Apple stock to its proprietary Leaderboard list on Wednesday morning. Leaderboard is available for free this week through Sunday night.
The Innovator's Dilemma Apple has grown by pursuing new technologies even if that means cannibalizing its own businesses, Munster said.
"Apple has embraced the innovator's dilemma unlike any other company in history," Munster said. That strategy "is best exemplified by the iPhone all but destroying the iPod business."
Apple today has a user base of 1.3 billion active devices, including over 810 million iPhones.
"In the future, the base of active devices will increasingly be made up of a mix of wearables (Apple Watch and Apple Glasses)," Munster said.
'Trillion Dollar Baby' Apple bull Brian White, an analyst with Monness Crespi Hardt, thinks Apple stock can run higher from here. He rates the stock as a buy with a 12-month price target of 275. At that target, Apple would have a market cap of $1.3 trillion.
"Despite today's significant accomplishment, we continue to believe Apple remains one of the most underappreciated stocks in the world with a valuation that remains depressed," White said in a report titled "Trillion Dollar Baby."
He added, "Now, Apple is heading into the seasonally strongest time of the year with a new iPhone cycle on the horizon."
